# Project structure {#sec-structure}

This page is the map of the repository. It lists every folder, says what belongs
in it, and shows which parts of the library may depend on which.

## The repository {.unnumbered}

```
main.py                     Entry point of the Qollab Python project.
qollab_api.py               The functions that Qollab pages call (they return text).
requirements.txt            Dependencies for Qollab (kept equal to pyproject.toml).
pyproject.toml              Packaging, dependencies and tool settings.
package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml   ESLint and the JS development tools (Node.js).
eslint.config.js            The ESLint configuration of the viewer.
Makefile                    The commands of the project (see Tooling and workflow).
.flake8                     The style rules of flake8.
.github/workflows/ci.yml    Continuous integration: lint and tests.
README.md, LICENSE          The overview of the project and its MIT license.
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md        The rules for code agents.

source/                     What is shipped: the library, the viewer and the tests.
  backend/                  The Python library.
    __init__.py             The public API: compile, export, load_circuit, sample.
    core/                   The modules (see below).
  frontend/                 The viewer.
    index.html              Markup only.
    styles.css              The style of the viewer (becomes main.css in the package).
    js/                     The ES modules of the viewer.
  shaders/                  GLSL: the Bloch spheres, laser, lens, phonon bus and rail.
  tests/                    The pytest suite, the shared circuits and the golden file.

resources/                  What supports the project.
  examples/                 Worked circuits (Bell, GHZ, layers, the QFT adder), the catalog of the selector and .qasm files.
  models/                   The laser model (OBJ and MTL).
  scripts/                  The demos, the generator of out/, the packager and the server.
  make/                     Makefile.git (branch workflow) and Makefile.quarto (this book).

documentation/              The specification, the schema and this book.
  _quarto.yml               The configuration of the book.
  docs/                     The chapters.
  diagrams/                 PlantUML sources and their SVG renders.
  schema/                   The JSON schema of the contract.
  internal/                 spec.md, memory.md, the working notes and the agent prompts.
  references/               Notes on the native gates of IonQ.

package.json, pnpm-lock.yaml   ESLint and the JavaScript development tools.
eslint.config.js            The ESLint configuration for the viewer.

out/                        Generated: the example JSON files and their manifest.
qollab/                     Generated: the project that is uploaded to Qollab.
documentation/_book/        Generated: the rendered book.
```

The three generated folders are not committed. `make outputs`, `make qollab` and
`make render` create them, and nothing in them is edited by hand.

## Why `source/` and `resources/` are separate {.unnumbered}

`source/` holds what the product is made of. `resources/` holds what is needed to
build, demonstrate or document it. The split has a practical effect: the setuptools
configuration looks in both (`where = ["source", "resources"]`), but it installs
only the packages `backend*` and `examples*`. The demos, the packager and the
server are therefore never installed with the library.

## The modules of the library {.unnumbered}

Everything under `source/backend/core/` follows one rule: a package per module, and
a public function whose name is a verb.

```
core/
  model.py          Frozen dataclasses that travel between the stages.
  errors.py         The exception hierarchy.
  constants.py      Values that never change (for example, a full turn).
  config.py         Values that policy may change (limits, decimals, timeouts).
  to_qiskit.py      A native circuit rebuilt as a QuantumCircuit.
  provider/         detect → BackendInfo; profiles.py holds the noise profiles.
  importer/         load_circuit: OpenQASM 2 or 3 → QuantumCircuit.
  transpiler/       transpile: the circuit changed to the gates of the backend.
  translator/       translate: normalize.py and rules.py produce only native gates.
  simulator/        simulate: one file per gate matrix, and the tomography.
  vectorizer/       vectorize: spherical angles to (x, y, z) vectors and probabilities.
  metrics/          measure: fidelity, inactivity, vibration and cost.
  formatter/        format: the dictionary of the contract.
  exporter/         export: the dictionary as JSON text.
  sampler/          sample: a simulated measurement of one step.
  compiler/         compile: runs the stages in order.
```

Each package has an `__init__.py` with one line, and one module file whose name is
the package name. Helpers sit next to it in the same package. For example, the
translator keeps its rules in `rules.py` and its pre-processing in `normalize.py`,
and the simulator keeps one matrix per file (`gpi.py`, `gpi2.py`, `ms.py`, `zz.py`,
`virtualz.py`).

## Module catalogue {.unnumbered}

What each module does, and where it sits in the flow. The pipeline modules are
those with an arrow in the last column.

| Module | Function | Role | In → out | Page |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `model` | (dataclasses) | Defines every object that travels between modules. | | [Data model](../modules/model.qmd) |
| `config`, `constants`, `errors` | | Limits and policy, fixed values, and the exception hierarchy. | | [Configuration and errors](../modules/config-and-errors.qmd) |
| `importer` | `load_circuit` | Reads an OpenQASM 2 or 3 text and explains what cannot be loaded. | text → `QuantumCircuit` | [Importer](../modules/importer.qmd) |
| `provider` | `detect` | Recognises IonQ Aria, IonQ Forte or the built-in simulator, picks the entangler and the noise profile. | backend → `BackendInfo` | [Provider](../modules/provider.qmd) |
| `transpiler` | `transpile` | Changes the circuit to the gates the backend understands; the single IonQ dry-run job is sent here. | circuit → `TranspiledCircuit` | [Transpiler](../modules/transpiler.qmd) |
| `translator` | `translate` | Rewrites every gate as GPI, GPI2, MS or ZZ, and virtual Z. | `TranspiledCircuit` → `NativeCircuit` | [Translator](../modules/translator.qmd) |
| `simulator` | `simulate` | Computes the exact state after every native gate and reduces it to one Bloch state per qubit. | `NativeCircuit` → `SimulatedCircuit` | [Simulator](../modules/simulator.qmd) |
| `simulator.tomography` | `measure` | Estimates those states from measurements instead of computing them. | `NativeCircuit` → `SimulatedCircuit` | [Tomography](../modules/tomography.qmd) |
| `vectorizer` | `vectorize` | Spherical angles to `(x, y, z)` and the probabilities `[p0, p1]`. | `SimulatedCircuit` → `VectorizedCircuit` | [Vectorizer](../modules/vectorizer.qmd) |
| `metrics` | `measure` | Adds fidelity, inactivity, vibration and cost. | `VectorizedCircuit` → `MeasuredCircuit` | [Metrics](../modules/metrics.qmd) |
| `formatter` | `format` | Builds the dictionary of the JSON contract. | `MeasuredCircuit` → `dict` | [Formatter and exporter](../modules/formatter-and-exporter.qmd) |
| `exporter` | `export` | Writes the dictionary as JSON text, or to a file. | `dict` → `str` | [Formatter and exporter](../modules/formatter-and-exporter.qmd) |
| `sampler` | `sample` | Draws the result of measuring a step from the JSON; applies the readout error. | `dict` → counts | [Sampler](../modules/sampler.qmd) |
| `to_qiskit` | `to_qiskit` | Rebuilds a native circuit as a `QuantumCircuit`; used by the tomography, the sampler and the tests. | `NativeCircuit` → `QuantumCircuit` | [Bridge to Qiskit](../modules/to-qiskit.qmd) |
| `compiler` | `compile` | Runs the pipeline in order and checks the arguments. | circuit and backend → `dict` | [Compiler](../modules/compiler.qmd) |

## Who may import whom {.unnumbered}

The imports of the library form a shallow tree. The table is read row by row: the
module in the first column may import the ones in the second column.

| Module | May import |
| --- | --- |
| `model`, `errors`, `constants`, `config` | Nothing from `core`. `model` uses Qiskit types. |
| `to_qiskit` | `model`, `constants` |
| `provider` | `model` |
| `importer` | `errors`, `config` |
| `transpiler` | `model`, `errors`, `config` |
| `translator` | `model`, `errors`, `constants` |
| `simulator` (and the tomography) | `model`, `errors`, `config`, `constants`, `to_qiskit` |
| `vectorizer` | `model` |
| `metrics`, `formatter` | `model`, `config` |
| `sampler` | `model`, `errors`, `config`, `constants`, `to_qiskit` |
| `exporter` | Nothing from `core` |
| `compiler` | Every stage, `model` and `errors` |

No arrow points from one stage to another. The only module with a wide view is
`compiler`. This has a direct benefit: a stage can be tested with a hand-made
input, without running the stages that come before it.

The adapters sit above the library and import only its public functions.

```
main.py ───────┐
               ├──► qollab_api.py ──► backend (compile, export, load_circuit, sample)
server.py ─────┘                          ▲
                                          └── examples/ (the circuits shown in the selector)
```

## Where the tests are {.unnumbered}

The suite lives in `source/tests/`, with one `test_<module>.py` per module. It
also covers the adapters and the tools (`test_qollab_api.py`, `test_server.py`,
`test_package_qollab.py`), the examples, the performance budget and the files that
keep the project consistent (`test_requirements.py` compares `requirements.txt`
with `pyproject.toml`, and `test_memory.py` keeps `documentation/internal/memory.md` short). See
[Tests](../development/tests.qmd).
